language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

I did not want to produce invented readings. The forms seen in some columns, such as small circles and dots beside letters, should be checked against the Manchu script before the language is confirmed. Rescanning at a higher resolution, or supplying a crop at full resolution, is recommended.</warning>

The left margin panel carries a short vertical-script label in about 4 segments, probably the title, volume and folio in Mongolian. There is light staining and some small losses along the bottom edge of the leaf.</meta>

translation.text:
<warning>The body text of this page was not transcribed because the image resolution was too low. No translation of the main text is possible. Only the Chinese margin label and the description of the frame are translated below.</warning>
<meta>The source page has about 20 vertical columns of red-ink text in the Uighur-Mongol script, set inside a decorated frame. The transcriber noted that the script might be Manchu rather than Classical Mongolian and that this should be checked. A rescan at higher resolution is recommended.</meta>

<margin>Great Jewel-Heap Sutra, Volume Two, upper folio three <note>original: "大寶積經第二卷上三". The Great Jewel-Heap Sutra, in Sanskrit the Mahāratnakūṭa-sūtra, is a large collection of Mahayana Buddhist scriptures. Chinese labels like this one were often printed in the margins of Mongolian Kanjur volumes from Beijing, so that the binders could keep the leaves in order.</note></margin>

<margin><unclear>short vertical-script margin label, about 4 words (probably title, volume and folio), not transcribed</unclear></margin>

<note>A rectangular frame of double ruled lines, filled with continuous scrollwork, surrounds the text block. Two narrow panels at the ends hold the margin labels and have leaf-shaped ornaments in their corners.</note>

<unclear>about 20 columns of vertical-script text in red ink (Classical Mongolian as stated, Manchu not ruled out), not transcribed because the image resolution is too low</unclear>

<summary>This is folio three of volume two of the Great Jewel-Heap Sutra (Mahāratnakūṭa-sūtra), probably from the Mongolian Kanjur printed in Beijing in 1718–20. Only the Chinese margin label and the decorative frame could be described. The main text was not transcribed.</summary>
